title: Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found two public GEO series (gene expression/genomics archive) by text search, since PubMed elink returned none: GSE311782 (24 samples, Repli-C, a contact-mapping method for newly copied DNA) and GSE311634 (20 samples, Micro-C, a high-resolution genome contact map). Listed both folders: the processed data are .hic/.mcool contact matrices of 0.3–3.9 GB each, with RAW tars of 37 GB and 23 GB. Downloaded and parsed the only small tables: GSE311782_fountains_all_conditions.tsv.gz has 14,982 rows of 'fountain' (origin-centred contact pattern) calls with coordinates across 9 conditions (e.g. UNT 2,082, HU 2,344, UNT_Auxin 3,012), all Type=Origin, plus one repeated header row embedded mid-file. GSE311634_loops_25_WT.tsv.gz has 4,541 loop calls and _SMC1kd has 346, each with score, p-value and q-value columns.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (paywalled; no PMCID, no full text or supplement in Europe PMC). The biological claims (cohesin accumulates at stalled forks, limits sister-fork coupling, PRIMPOL involvement) and the fork-speed/reversal measurements (DNA fiber assays, electron microscopy) were not seen in any deposited table.

a1_downloadable.note: Both GEO series are public over FTP with no login; checked the directory listings and downloaded three small TSVs.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No per-item measured outcome table exists. The only tables are positive-only lists of loops and fountains called by peak-calling software. Any label (for example, whether a contact gains or loses under HU, a drug that stalls replication, or after cohesin removal) would have to be built by calling features yourself from multi-GB .hic matrices and matching them across conditions.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be genomic coordinates (hg38, implied), with sequence or chromatin features fetched from outside sources. Fork-level measurements such as speed and reversal are not deposited at all.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates are in base pairs, with resolution stated in a 'res' column (10,000 or 25,000). Loop scores are unitless calling-tool statistics.

a5_enough_rows.note: 14,982 fountain calls in total, but these are only positives, spread across 9 conditions and about 2,397 distinct IDs. Negatives would have to be constructed.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: About 10–25 GB of .hic files to re-derive contacts across conditions
a6_fits_laptop.note: Building any real label means reading several 2–3 GB .hic matrices. That is feasible by streaming one chromosome at a time, but slow, and it lands at genomics scale.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts were available to compare, because only the abstract could be read. The file sample counts (24 and 20) match the GEO metadata.

a8_label_provenance.note: The fountain and loop calls are outputs of feature-calling algorithms run on the contact maps. They are not direct measurements, and a model predicting them would learn the caller's behaviour.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome (DNA model with contact-map outputs) would be the natural fit if a label existed

integration.partner_dataset: 4DN (4D Nucleome) Micro-C/Hi-C collections, and ENCODE replication timing
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether DNA sequence and chromatin state predict which replication origins rewire their contacts under replication stress; not pursued because no label table exists.

honest_claim_h3: A model could only claim to reproduce the output of a contact-feature caller at origins in one human cell line, across 9 conditions with no negatives; that is not a measured biological outcome.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence around replication origins to predict which origins change their 3D contacts when DNA copying is stalled.
plain_idea.train_on: Genomic windows around origins, each with a sequence and a condition (untreated or drug-stalled, cohesin present or removed); about 14,982 called positive features, and no negatives deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Whether an origin-centred contact pattern is called in a given condition. The answer comes from peak-calling software run on Repli-C contact maps, not from a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers studying replication stress could see which genome regions depend on cohesin to protect stalled forks, which bears on cancers with cohesin mutations.

ml_idea: Predict, from sequence (for example with AlphaGenome embeddings), which origins form condition-specific Repli-C fountains. Rejected: the label is a positive-only list of algorithm calls, and negatives or differential labels would have to be rebuilt from 2–3 GB .hic matrices.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed. Working set assumes about 6 condition-merged .hic files of 2–3 GB each, streamed one chromosome at a time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether any deposited table records a measured per-locus or per-fork outcome. Already done: none exists; only feature calls and contact matrices are deposited.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic cell-biology paper whose deposited data are multi-GB contact matrices plus positive-only lists of algorithm-called loops and fountains (14,982 rows). No measured label column exists (A2), labels come from calling software (A8), and building a real label needs 10–25 GB of .hic processing (A6).
